cf.title: BUG #19737: Empty `JSON_OBJECT` cannot use documented `ON NULL` or unique-key clauses

input.subject: BUG #19737: Empty `JSON_OBJECT` cannot use documented `ON NULL` or unique-key clauses

verdict_reasoning: The doc mismatch is real, but the thread shows no query that needs ON NULL or UNIQUE with an empty list (demand-1). Message #1 itself says the clauses do not change the result, and JSON_OBJECT() already returns {}. The docs-only fix from message #2 matches the current parser and was never weighed against the grammar change. The list should choose between the two fixes before code review.

brief.title: Allow on null and unique-key clauses in empty JSON_OBJECT and JSON_ARRAY
brief.problem: The docs show the key/value list of JSON_OBJECT as optional and independent of the ON NULL, UNIQUE and RETURNING clauses. But JSON_OBJECT(ABSENT ON NULL) and JSON_OBJECT(WITH UNIQUE KEYS) fail with a syntax error, while JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_OBJECT(RETURNING jsonb) work. JSON_ARRAY(NULL ON NULL) fails the same way.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds grammar productions in gram.y so that empty JSON_OBJECT accepts the NULL/ABSENT ON NULL, WITH/WITHOUT UNIQUE KEYS and RETURNING clauses, and empty JSON_ARRAY accepts ON NULL and RETURNING. Each such call returns an empty object or array. v3 also notes in func-json.sgml and the commit message that this differs from the SQL standard grammar.
user_visible_surface: SQL syntax: JSON_OBJECT( { NULL | ABSENT } ON NULL ) and JSON_OBJECT( { WITH | WITHOUT } UNIQUE [ KEYS ] ) with no key/value pairs now parse.
SQL syntax: JSON_ARRAY( { NULL | ABSENT } ON NULL [ RETURNING ... ] ) with no values now parses.
Documentation: func-json.sgml gets notes on the difference from the SQL standard.
author_claims: The parser contradicts the documented syntax, so this is a bug fix.
The new gram.y productions add no grammar conflicts.
Regression tests in sqljson.sql cover all clause combinations for empty objects.
The SQL:2016 grammar nests the ON NULL and uniqueness clauses inside the required key/value list, so Postgres's documented syntax differs from the standard.
A reviewer reports that Oracle and other systems accept the empty forms, based on an LLM search.
brief.thread_state: Nitin Motiani tested v1 and v2, asked for JSON_ARRAY coverage and for the standard difference to be documented, and v3 does both. No committer has replied, and jian he's earlier idea of fixing only the docs got no follow-up.
unclear: The thread does not show the v3 documentation text or commit message, so reviewers cannot judge how the standard difference is described.
Nobody discussed the alternative of fixing the docs to match the standard instead of extending the grammar.
The thread does not say whether the fix should be back-patched or is for master only.
The thread does not show regression tests for the JSON_ARRAY empty forms.
No one checked other SQL/JSON constructors, such as JSON_OBJECTAGG or JSON_ARRAYAGG, for the same gap.

objections.title: No use case shown for clauses that cannot change the result
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres adds grammar for JSON_OBJECT(ABSENT ON NULL) and similar forms, which always return {} or []. If no user needs them, the project still carries syntax that the SQL:2016 grammar does not allow. A later standard revision or other systems may define these forms differently, and Postgres must then keep its own behavior or break callers.
objections.argument: The only demand in the thread is the doc mismatch in message #1, and message #1 itself says the clauses do not change the result. Anyone who hits the error can drop the clause, since JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_ARRAY() already work (message #3, message #7). Message #2 offers a docs-only fix that matches the standard, and nobody weighed it against the grammar change. Message #9 calls the grammar change "probably" right only because the docs already differ from the standard.
objections.author_must_show: Which real queries or SQL generators emit ON NULL or UNIQUE clauses with an empty list, and why is dropping the clause or fixing the docs not enough for them?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows one bug report and no query or SQL generator that needs the clauses with an empty list, and message #1 says they do not change the result. P10 is about a new keyword and must not be used as support.

other_surviving.title: Grammar extended beyond the standard when a docs fix would close the bug
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user writes JSON_OBJECT(ABSENT ON NULL RETURNING jsonb) in a generator or ORM template because Postgres accepts it. The same template is later run on a system that follows the SQL:2016 grammar and fails with a syntax error. Postgres has then added a non-standard spelling whose clauses have no effect on the result.
other_surviving.argument: Message #6 shows that SQL:2016 makes the null clause and the uniqueness clause depend on at least one name/value pair, and message #9 agrees the patch departs from the standard. Message #2 offered a docs-only fix that matches the standard and the current parser, and nobody weighed it against the grammar change. Message #9 says "since the documentation is already different", so documentation wording is the stated reason for the departure from the standard. The only evidence that other systems accept the empty forms is an LLM search in message #5.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why should the parser change to accept clauses that have no effect and that the standard grammar rejects, when correcting the json_object and json_array synopses would match both the standard and current behaviour?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 shows the parser already follows the SQL:2016 grammar, and message #2's docs-only fix was never weighed against the grammar change. The only evidence that other systems accept the empty forms is the LLM search in message #5.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: New syntax in a back-patched bug fix splits minor releases
other_surviving.failure_scenario: The fix is back-patched to 18.x. A user on 18.7 creates a view using JSON_ARRAY(NULL ON NULL). A dump of that view then fails to restore on an 18.5 server, and the same query fails on a standby that runs an older minor release. The user sees this only at restore time or after a failover.
other_surviving.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix and the thread frames the change as a bug, which suggests back-patching. Message #10 does not say whether the change targets master only. New accepted syntax in a minor release means that SQL and dumps written on a newer minor release can fail on an older one. A docs-only fix carries no such risk.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Is this grammar change meant for master only, and if it is to be back-patched, how are SQL and dumps that use the new forms handled on older minor releases?

critic.reasoning: The entry is tagged Bugfix and the thread does not say whether the change is for master only. New accepted syntax in a minor release can fail on an older-minor standby, so the question is fair and a one-line answer settles it.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Grammar extension beyond the standard, with the docs-only fix not weighed
refuted.failure_scenario: The patch is back-patched as a bug fix. A user writes JSON_OBJECT(ABSENT ON NULL) on 18.7, and the query fails on 18.6 replicas and on other standard-conforming systems. Postgres now carries a permanent non-standard form that it cannot remove later without breaking these queries.
refuted.argument: Message #6 shows the SQL:2016 grammar nests the ON NULL and uniqueness clauses inside the required key/value list, so the parser follows the standard and the docs are what is wrong. jian he's docs-only fix in message #2 keeps the standard grammar and got no follow-up. Message #9 accepts the extension only because the docs already differ. A committer would likely ask why a documentation error should be fixed by adding permanent syntax, and why it is filed as a back-patchable bug.
refuted.author_must_show: What user need do the empty forms with ON NULL or UNIQUE serve that a corrected synopsis would not, and is the grammar change meant for master only?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the docs-only alternative and of standards-compat-2 for back-patching. It adds no separate point.

refuted.title: Separate empty-form productions must track every future constructor clause
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a clause to JSON_OBJECT or JSON_ARRAY, for example a new output option. The author updates the non-empty production only. The empty form then rejects the new clause, the docs and parser disagree again, and nobody notices until a new bug report arrives.
refuted.argument: Message #4 says the patch adds new productions for the empty case and does not make the list optional in the existing rule. This bug exists because two rules diverged: RETURNING was allowed in the empty form but ON NULL was not. Duplicating the clause lists sets up the same divergence for every future clause, with no test that fails if one list is missed.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the grammar make the key/value list optional inside one rule so each clause is listed once, or what keeps the empty and non-empty forms in sync later?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a future constructor clause that nobody has proposed. Message #3 shows the empty form already takes RETURNING separately, and message #6 shows that split comes from the standard grammar, so the patch follows existing practice.

refuted.title: Empty forms already work by dropping clauses that have no effect
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who wants an empty object or array writes JSON_OBJECT() or JSON_ARRAY(RETURNING jsonb), and both work today. Under the patch, gram.y carries extra productions for forms that give the same result and that the SQL:2016 grammar does not allow. Each later change to the SQL/JSON constructor grammar must keep these productions conflict-free.
refuted.argument: Messages #1 and #3 agree that ON NULL and UNIQUE do not change the result when there are no pairs, and that JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_OBJECT(RETURNING jsonb) already return {}. So the new syntax adds no result that cannot be had today. Message #2 proposed fixing the docs to match the parser, which keeps Postgres aligned with the standard grammar that message #6 quotes. Message #9 accepts the grammar change only because the docs already differ, and nobody compared the two fixes on their merits.
refuted.author_must_show: What real query, such as SQL generated by a tool, needs the ON NULL or UNIQUE clause with no pairs, and why is fixing the docs not enough for it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1 for the missing use case and of standards-compat-1 for the docs-only alternative. P10 concerns a new MAP keyword and expression type, so it does not support this point.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch accepts empty JSON_OBJECT and JSON_ARRAY forms with ON NULL and UNIQUE clauses that the SQL:2016 grammar does not allow.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A view written with the new forms may dump as text that an older minor release cannot parse, if the fix is back-patched.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix against 18.6, and the thread does not say whether the grammar change is for master only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: New gram.y productions for the empty forms must stay conflict-free and stay accepted in every later release.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_ARRAY() without the clauses already return the same empty object or array.

questions: Which real queries or SQL generators emit ON NULL or UNIQUE clauses with an empty key/value list, and why is dropping the clause not enough for them?
Why is the grammar change better than the docs-only fix from message #2, which matches both the current parser and the SQL:2016 grammar?
Is the grammar change meant for master only, or for back-patching to the supported branches?
If it is back-patched, what happens to SQL and dumps that use the new forms on an older minor release?
Do JSON_OBJECTAGG and JSON_ARRAYAGG have the same gap between the documented synopsis and the parser?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the SQL/JSON constructor grammar in gram.y and the SQL/JSON standard text would have to own it. None has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for syntax beyond SQL:2016 that Postgres must accept in every later release, and for any conflict with a later standard revision.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 and v3 in response to review, adding JSON_ARRAY coverage and a note on the difference from the standard.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A real query, ORM or SQL generator that emits these clauses with an empty list, or documentation from other database systems showing they accept the empty forms. The LLM search in message #5 does not count as this evidence.

priority.reason: The patch touches only gram.y, the regression tests and func-json.sgml, and the new forms return what JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_ARRAY() already return. The thread first needs to choose between this grammar change and the docs-only fix from message #2.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can confirm that the new gram.y productions add no conflicts, or how a view that uses the new forms is deparsed. The v3 documentation text on the difference from the standard is not shown.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
Reverted commit(s): JSON_TABLE PLAN clause
precedents_retrieved.objection:
86ab7f4c721d commit made the table-level ON ERROR clause serve as the default
ON ERROR for columns lacking their own, so that a top-level ERROR ON ERROR
turned per-column evaluation errors into hard errors.

The SQL standard does mandate this cascade, but introducing it should be
a deliberate, separately-documented change, so restore the previous
behavior for now.  This also reverts the paired ruleutils.c logic that
deparsed a column's behavior against an ERROR default: that dropped an
explicit ERROR ON EMPTY from a dumped view, and otherwise emitted a
redundant NULL ON EMPTY.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to), and in v2 json_translate, which recursively replaces every value, including array elements, that exactly equals a given string with another string. The author meant it for mapping categorical or enum values deep inside a document, in the style of the Unix tr utility.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Blindly replacing every
instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche
use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?

precedents_retrieved.title: Add SQL syntax check
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a --syntax option to the postgres server binary that reads SQL from standard input, runs it through the raw parser only (no catalog access or parse analysis), and reports whether it is valid SQL via a message and exit code. The intent was to support manual and automated script checks and editor integrations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Several reviewers held that the feature did not belong in the postgres binary, and Robert Haas marked the entry Rejected on that basis. The main objection, attributed to Tom Lane and endorsed by Robert Haas, was that the check exposes an implementation detail, the division of work between gram.y (raw_parser) and parse analysis, so it would miss things users consider syntax errors and flag things that seem semantic. Making that work would need a much larger effort and a different design. Robert Haas also noted that the 45-line patch had no comments, tests or documentation, and the author agreed to the rejection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I strongly suspect that doing something useful in this area requires
about two orders of magnitude more code than are included in this
patch, and a completely different design.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert 95d737ff to add 'ignore_nulls'
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert 95d737ff to add 'ignore_nulls'
Reverted commit(s): Add 'ignore_nulls' option to row_to_json
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Per discussion, revert the commit which added 'ignore_nulls' to
row_to_json.  This capability would be better added as an independent
function rather than being bolted on to row_to_json.  Additionally,
the implementation didn't address complex JSON objects, and so was
incomplete anyway.

Pointed out by Tom and discussed with Andrew and Robert.

precedents_retrieved.title: Ltree syntax improvement
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the set of characters allowed in ltree labels by adding two escaping mechanisms, backslash-escaping of individual characters and double-quoting of whole labels, for the ltree, lquery and ltxtquery datatypes. Later versions refactored the label parsing into common code shared by the three types.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to the design of having both quoting and backslash-escaping and proposed SQL-identifier-style quoting instead. He also questioned the stripping of leading and trailing whitespace, the structure of ltree_io.c (several routines that depend on the quoting rules and must stay in sync, plus multiple passes over the input), and changes to error reporting. After a later request to rebase, no new version was submitted for two months, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As I mentioned upthread, I'm not convinced that we ought to have
*both* quoting and backslash-escaping in these datatypes.

precedents_retrieved.title: skip empty transactions for logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change pgoutput so it defers the BEGIN message until a transaction produces a change to send, and drops BEGIN and COMMIT for transactions that touch no published tables. The goal is to cut network traffic when most upstream transactions only modify unpublished tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. The patch no longer applied and stayed in Waiting on Author for about six weeks, so it was marked Returned with feedback. Open design questions were never resolved: Craig Ringer noted that skipping empty transactions can delay synchronous replication feedback, and Andres Freund proposed a lighter progress message or rate limiting instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Since then, the patch is failing to apply, waiting on author and the thread has died 6 weeks or so ago, so I am marking it as RwF in the CF.

precedents_retrieved.title: Boolean partition syntax
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the grammar of the partition FOR VALUES clause so that the Boolean literals true and false are accepted as partition bound values, which previously produced a syntax error. Later in the thread a broader alternative was posted that restricts partition bounds to the AexprConst grammar and coerces them during parse analysis.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The discussion moved from the narrow Boolean-literal fix to whether partition bounds should be parsed more generally, for example as expressions evaluated and checked for constancy, and senior developers disagreed with the patch's design. The alternative AexprConst-based patch was not reviewed and was found to reject negative numbers. With the final commitfest in progress and no updated patch, the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Given the current state of this patch, with a number of senior
developers disagreeing with the design, and the last CF being in
progress, I think we should mark this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: MAP syntax for arrays
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Andreas Karlsson, Ashutosh Bapat
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a new expression type and syntax MAP(<func_name> OVER <array_expression>) that applies a function to each element of an array and returns the resulting array, reusing the existing array-coercion infrastructure. The author also considered a more general form mapping an arbitrary expression over an array, and reported better performance than the unnest/array_agg subquery approach for small arrays.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected to adding proprietary syntax that could conflict with future SQL standard use of the MAP keyword, which is already a non-reserved keyword in SQL:2016. They also judged the syntax not much better than the existing sub-select with unnest and array_agg, which is more flexible (for example, it allows a WHERE filter), and suggested optimizing the unnest/array_agg combination in the planner instead of adding new syntax. Heikki Linnakangas summarized the consensus as not wanting the feature and marked the entry Rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Yeah, it's a
handy syntax, but it's not that much better than using a subselect or a
writing a user-defined function. And there's risk of future conflicts
with the SQL standard.

precedents_retrieved.title: json_table function PLAN clause
precedents_retrieved.authors: Amit Langote (amitlan), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Nikita Malakhov (nmalakh)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the SQL-standard PLAN clause to JSON_TABLE, which lets the user choose how NESTED paths are joined to their parent and siblings. It builds on the committed JSON_TABLE code and also corrects some earlier JSON_TABLE tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Amit Langote and Alexander Korotkov asked for missing documentation, separation of refactoring from new code, and fixes to IsA() use, deparsing and test coverage. The author answered these in v23 four days before the entry was withdrawn, and no message explains the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow foreign keys to reference a superset of unique columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow a foreign key constraint to reference a set of columns that is a superset of the columns of a non-deferrable unique or primary key index on the referenced table, rather than requiring an exact match. An optional USING INDEX clause after the referenced column list would name the supporting unique index where the choice would otherwise be ambiguous.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the semantics are questionable (for example CASCADE behaviour of the extra columns, nullable subset columns, MATCH PARTIAL and UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT), that the change could break existing optimizations, and that it risks conflict with the SQL standard and its information_schema. He said a patch was premature unless the SQL committee standardized the behaviour. Peter Eisentraut said that working out the full specification was the open work still required of the proposal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the semantics are at best questionable, I think
it will break important optimizations, and I think the chances of
finding ourselves in conflict with some future SQL spec extension are
too high.

precedents_retrieved.title: Indeterminate behavior for the GROUP BY clause
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Indeterminate behavior for the GROUP BY clause
Section: Features We Do Not Want
Linked: Re: SQL compatibility reminder: MySQL vs PostgreSQL
precedents_retrieved.objection: At least one other database product allows specification of a subset of the result columns which GROUP BY would need to be able to provide predictable results; the server is free to return any value from the group. This is not viewed as a desirable feature. PostgreSQL 9.1 allows result columns that are not referenced by GROUP BY if a primary key for the same table is referenced in GROUP BY.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent rejected this idea. P10's standard-conflict concern applies only weakly, because the patch adds no keyword and no new semantics. Within the thread, message #2 proposed a docs-only fix that nobody pursued, and messages #9 and #10 already weighed the difference from the standard, so no prior reason stands unanswered.
Two objections are raised. The listed precedents concern new proprietary syntax with new meaning, while this change only accepts clauses that have no effect, so they are not cited.

The change adds parser productions and doc text only. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, wire message or struct change, and the parse tree it builds is the existing empty constructor node. A view using the new forms stores that node and is deparsed by the existing ruleutils code. Whether that deparsed text parses on older minor releases, if back-patched, cannot be checked without the code.

The proposal only adds grammar productions so that empty JSON_OBJECT and JSON_ARRAY accept ON NULL, unique-key and RETURNING clauses, and each such call returns an empty object or array. It adds no privilege, role, data access, information exposure or resource-use path, so there is no security angle to object on.
Hot-path cost is nil: this is parse-time grammar only. No external dependencies or catalog changes are involved.
One objection only. No extension or other feature is relevant, because JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_ARRAY() without clauses already produce the result the proposal wants.
One fixable demand objection. The doc mismatch is a real bug, but the thread shows no user who needs the empty forms.
